Switzerland is voting to prescribe gym by doctors

Ehh no this is an article about a group that planning to start collecting signatures (An inititiative needs to gather 100'000 signatures in 18 months to be valid). There is no exact text yet and their intent is most likely to have gym subscriptions be covered by health insurance if it's prescribed by a doctor. Also initiatives are highly unlikely (11% of all initiatives that were being voted on passed the popular vote) to pass and this one doesn't seem likely to pass even if they manage to get enough signatures.

I think that fitness centers should absolutely be covered by medical, but regardless of being prescribed by a doctor. Everyone can benefit from access to facilities and it might make people more likely to start if they no longer have to commit to spending a lot at the beginning.

But how do you regulate something like this? As much as I agree that everyone should have access to some form of physical exercise, why can't people be prescribed to go running instead? Or push ups or sit ups? If everyone started getting free memberships to Holme's Place for the hammam, it would be a useless drain on the government's funds.
